research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9538 at 10 FR 4057, in the Federal Register of April 17, 1945 (govinfo file FR-1945-04-17, PDF page 1; text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The masthead date line in the OCR text layer is garbled and is not used. The order is headed Executive Order 9538, is signed April 13, 1945, and its filing line reads Filed, Apr. 14, 1945. Text and inventory: one operative paragraph, confirmed as one clause. Under section 1753 of the Revised Statutes and section 2 of the Civil Service Act, it authorizes the Civil Service Commission to certify for probational appointment any person whose name was on a list of eligibles between May 1, 1940 and March 16, 1942 (for the field service of the Post Office Department, October 23, 1943), who entered the armed forces between those dates and was honorably separated and remains qualified, who stood higher on the list than another applicant who received a probational appointment, and who asks for restoration or certification within ninety days after the end of military service or of hospitalization continuing after discharge for not more than one year, or within ninety days after the date of the order, whichever is later. A proviso excludes cases in which the list had expired before the applicant entered the armed forces and the Commission had not sustained objections to his certification because of his draft status. Ending: Executive Order 9733, signed June 4, 1946 and printed at 11 FR 6127 in the Federal Register of June 6, 1946 (held govinfo text layer), states in paragraph 3 that it supersedes Executive Order "No. 9538 of April 13, 1945", naming it also by title. Its paragraph 1 authorizes and directs the Commission to certify the same four classes on the same conditions and proviso, and paragraph 2 adds further classes. Executive Order 9733 has no effective-date wording, so the end is dated on signing, 1946-06-04; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the filing date (June 4, 1946) and publication date (June 6, 1946) are not used. Later event: Part III of Executive Order 9830, signed February 24, 1947 and printed at 12 FR 1259, lists "No. 9538 of April 13, 1945." among the orders revoked; its enacting clause reads "it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:". That revocation fell on an order already superseded and is recorded as a later event, not as the first end. Executive Order 9598 of August 17, 1945 states that it "does not supersede or modify Executive Order No. 9538 of April 13, 1945", so it is a recital that leaves the order unchanged and is disclosed in a source note. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records the Executive Order 9733 supersession, the Executive Order 9830 revocation and a cross-reference between this order and Executive Order 9598. The held-text number search found this number in the texts of Executive Orders 9598 and 9733, in Federal Register text files of the order's own issue and of the Executive Order 9598 issue, and in a Civil Service Commission cross-reference printed with Executive Order 9733.
savings_reason: Paragraph 1 of Executive Order 9733 re-enacts the same certification authority on the same conditions, so the function continued under that separate order; certifications already made under Executive Order 9538 are completed acts. Executive Order 9733 contains no wording that preserves Executive Order 9538 itself.
earlier_end_check: Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The ninety-day period is the time within which each applicant must ask for restoration or certification; it runs from the later of the end of that person's service or hospitalization and the date of the order, so it gives no fixed end of the authorization. (2) Executive Order 9598 of August 17, 1945 expressly does not supersede or modify the order. (3) No instrument before Executive Order 9733 revokes or supersedes the order, and no held source shows the authorization exhausted before then: the OFR disposition notes record only the Executive Order 9598 cross-reference, the Executive Order 9733 supersession and the Executive Order 9830 revocation.
scope_check: One clause. Executive Order 9733 supersedes the order as a whole, naming it by number, date and title, without limitation. The dossier note asking that the large actor text of Executive Order 9830 be read is satisfied: I read its enacting clause, Part III and its signature block in the held Federal Register text; Part III revokes the listed orders without exception, and the ACT record notes no saving wording in that text.
independent_command_check: The order has one command, the certification authority with its conditions and proviso. It has no separate command; the same authority continued under paragraph 1 of Executive Order 9733.
savings_check: No wording in Executive Order 9733 preserves Executive Order 9538. The authority continued under Executive Order 9733 paragraph 1 as a new command (state continuing_independent), and certifications made before June 4, 1946 are completed acts.

research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10103 at 15 FR 597, in the Federal Register of February 3, 1950 (PDF page 3; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The page header in the held text reads 597 with the date Friday, February 3, 1950; the order is headed Executive Order 10103, Amendment of Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946, Providing for the Transfer of Personnel to Certain Public International Organizations, and is signed February 1, 1950. The held page also prints neighbouring documents, which are outside the inventory. Text and inventory: an enacting paragraph amending Executive Order 9721 and two numbered amendments, recorded as three clauses. Amendment 1 adds to section 1 of Executive Order 9721, effective as of May 10, 1946, a sentence beginning "Any employee so transferred shall, for a period not to exceed three years from the date of transfer", which treats a transferred employee as on leave of absence from federal employment while employed by the organization, provided he is later reemployed under section 3. Amendment 2 revives section 2 of Executive Order 9721, which had become inoperative on May 10, 1949, effective as of that date, and restates it: it gives competitive status to certain transferred war-service indefinite employees, and treats employees serving in an organization on September 30, 1949 as in active-duty status on that date for the purposes of Executive Order No. 10080. Partial revocation in 1959: section 2 of Executive Order 10804, signed February 12, 1959 and printed at 24 FR 1147 in the Federal Register of February 14, 1959 (held govinfo text layer), lists Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946, Executive Order No. 10103 of February 1, 1950, and Executive Order No. 10774 of July 25, 1958, the last "insofar as it affects any employee covered by section 6(a) of the International Atomic" Energy Agency Participation Act of 1957; the singular qualifier attaches to Executive Order 10774 alone. All three are revoked, except that "each shall be considered to remain in effect with respect to any" employee subject to it who was serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act and does not elect coverage under section 6 of that Act, and "for the purposes of any rights and benefits vested under each such order prior to the date of the enactment of the" Act. Executive Order 10103 was therefore revoked generally in 1959 but remained in effect for those two saved classes. Later presidential orders applied it as still in effect for saved employees: Executive Order 11138, signed January 7, 1964 (29 FR 225), and Executive Order 11303 (31 FR 11963, filed September 12, 1966) each modify Executive Order 9721 as amended by Executive Order 10103 by waiving the section 1 leave-of-absence limit for one named employee. The editorial note under 22 U.S.C. 288 found by the machine U.S. Code search likewise records that the orders were revoked with certain savings provisions by section 2 of Executive Order 10804 and subsequently revoked by Executive Order 12553. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10103 with the subject "Amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. The table also lists 9721. That revocation, without exception, is the first end of the saved remainder and so of the whole order. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records the 1959 revocation in part by Executive Order 10804, the Executive Order 11138 and 11303 modifications, the Executive Order 12553 revocation and a cross-reference to Executive Order 10080. The held-text number search found this number in the texts of Executive Orders 10804, 11138 and 11303, in Federal Register text files of the order's own issue, and in a Civil Service Commission regulation's authority citation.
savings_reason: Leave-of-absence status, reemployment rights and competitive status that employees acquired under the order are accrued effects. Section 2 of Executive Order 10804 keeps the order in effect for the purposes of rights and benefits vested before the enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act; the enacting sentence of Executive Order 12553 has no saving clause. No held source shows a continuing command of the order after 1986-02-25.
earlier_end_check: Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) Section 2 of Executive Order 10804 (signed 1959-02-12) revokes Executive Order 10103 generally, but provides that it remains in effect for employees serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act who do not elect coverage under that Act, and for rights and benefits vested before that date. Because the order stayed in effect for those classes, the 1959 revocation did not end it entirely; it is recorded as a later event on each clause. Executive Orders 11138 (1964) and 11303 (1966) show the President still applying the order, as amended, to saved employees, and no held source shows the saved classes extinguished before 1986. (2) Executive Orders 11138 and 11303 waive a time limit for one named employee each; they are modifications, not ends. (3) The three-year limits in the order run separately for each employee from that employee's transfer, so they supply no fixed end of the order. (4) The Federal Employees International Organization Service Act (72 Stat. 961) is not held, so no statutory replacement is claimed as an end. Executive Order 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes the order without exception.
scope_check: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, together with Executive Order 9721 and any amendments thereto, without exception, so it reaches all three clauses and the remainder saved in 1959. The dossier leads are resolved. The held text of Executive Order 10080 does not mention Executive Order 10103 or 9721; this order refers to 10080, not the reverse, so 10080 acts on nothing here. Executive Orders 11138 and 11303 each waive the section 1 leave-of-absence limit, which is the sentence added by amendment 1 of this order, for one named employee (Frederick Strauss and Reginald C. Price); they are recorded as later events on that clause and revoke nothing. Executive Order 11138 also waives the reemployment limit in section 3(a), which is part of Executive Order 9721's own text and not of this order's inventory.
independent_command_check: Amendment 1 (leave of absence for up to three years while employed by the organization, if the employee is later reemployed under section 3) and amendment 2 (competitive status for certain transferred war-service employees, and active-duty status on September 30, 1949 for the purposes of Executive Order 10080) are separate amendments of Executive Order 9721. Each is an amendment of the same parent and, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments, continues, amended, until the parent ends; Executive Order 12553 revokes the parent and this order together. None has its own end shown in held evidence.
savings_check: Accrued leave-of-absence status, reemployment rights and competitive status survive as accrued effects (state transferred_or_accrued). Section 2 of Executive Order 10804 preserved vested rights and benefits when it revoked the order in 1959; the enacting sentence of Executive Order 12553 has no saving or exception clause.

research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10138 at 15 FR 4241, in the Federal Register of July 4, 1950 (PDF page 3; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The page header in the held text reads FEDERAL REGISTER 4241 with the date Tuesday, July 4, 1950; the order is headed Executive Order 10138, is signed July 3, 1950, and its filing line reads Filed, July 3, 1950. The same page also prints Executive Order 10139, which concerns the Toledo Lakefront Dock Company. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Toledo, Lorain & Fairport Dock Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, A. F. of L.; invoking section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, it states "I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate the said dispute." It provides that no member of the board may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier, directs the board to report its findings to the President "within thirty days from the date of this order", and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported "no change, except by agreement, shall be made" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10138 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10138_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10138_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_ba0763e74c.txt, PDF page 1) is titled as the report of the emergency board appointed July 3, 1950 by Executive Orders 10138 and 10139, and its title page is dated at Toledo, Ohio, August 11, 1950. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in Federal Register text files of the same issue (the files for Executive Orders 10136 to 10139 hold the same pages), a Federal Register codification guide for page 4241, and the front matter of the board's report.
